questions.question: Day 15 Practice (Polite Social Manners (Phase 2)): When talking about booking an auto ride (this evening), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My colleague'?

options.a: I am booking an auto ride right now.
options.b: Please drop me off near gate 2 of the metro station.
options.c: Drop me station gate. yesterday
options.d: Drop me station gate.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Please drop me off near gate 2 of the metro station.".

questions.question: Day 15 Vocabulary (Polite Social Manners (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'iron out'?

options.a: Resolve minor problems or details in a plan.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'iron out' means: resolve minor problems or details in a plan. Example: "We need one final sync to iron out contract details."

options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:

'drop off' means: take someone to a destination and leave them there. Example: "Please drop me off near the bus stand."

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 1 (Polite Social Manners (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.

questions.question:
Day 15 Translation Scenario 2 (Polite Social Manners (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.b: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.
